title: Cryptocurrency & Blockchain Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to maximize your cryptocurrency privacy and blockchain anonymity. Protect your crypto transactions from tracking and surveillance.
intro: Cryptocurrency transactions are permanently recorded on public blockchains, making privacy protection essential. This checklist covers practical steps to enhance your crypto privacy, from choosing privacy-focused coins to securing your transaction methods.

items.task: Use Incognito Browser for all crypto activities
items.why: Standard browsers leak data that can link your identity to crypto addresses through tracking scripts and fingerprinting.
items.howTo: Download Incognito Browser and use it exclusively for cryptocurrency exchanges, wallets, and research. Never mix crypto activities with regular browsing.

items.task: Connect through VPN or Tor network
items.why: Your IP address can be linked to blockchain transactions, revealing your location and potentially your identity to observers.
items.howTo: Use a no-logs VPN service or Tor browser before accessing any crypto services. For maximum privacy, use VPN + Tor combination.

items.why: WebRTC can leak your real IP address even when using a VPN, compromising your location privacy.
items.howTo: In browser settings, disable WebRTC or use browser extensions like WebRTC Leak Shield to block WebRTC requests completely.

items.why: Custodial exchanges require KYC verification and can freeze funds, while privacy wallets offer better transaction anonymity features.
items.howTo: Choose wallets like Wasabi, Samourai (Bitcoin) or official Monero wallet. Avoid exchange wallets for long-term storage.

items.task: Generate new receiving addresses for each transaction
items.why: Address reuse creates a transaction history that can be analyzed to reveal spending patterns and wallet balances.
items.howTo: Enable HD (Hierarchical Deterministic) wallets and use the 'generate new address' feature for every incoming payment.

items.task: Use coin mixing services for Bitcoin transactions
items.why: Bitcoin transactions are pseudonymous but traceable. Mixing breaks the transaction chain linking your addresses.
items.howTo: Use CoinJoin through Wasabi Wallet or Whirlpool through Samourai Wallet. Mix coins before major transactions.

items.why: Privacy coins like Monero and Zcash offer built-in transaction anonymity that Bitcoin lacks by design.
items.howTo: Research Monero (XMR), Zcash (ZEC), or Dash for private transactions. Use atomic swaps or privacy exchanges for conversion.

items.why: Centralized exchanges require identity verification and maintain transaction records that can be subpoenaed or hacked.
items.howTo: Use DEXs like Bisq, LocalMonero, or Uniswap that don't require KYC. Trade peer-to-peer when possible.

items.task: Separate KYC and non-KYC crypto activities
items.why: Mixing verified exchange coins with privacy activities can compromise your anonymity efforts.
items.howTo: Keep separate wallets for KYC exchange purchases and private transactions. Never directly transfer between them.

items.why: Consistent transaction patterns in timing and amounts can be used to identify and track your wallet activity.
items.howTo: Vary transaction times, use random delays, and avoid round numbers. Don't empty wallets in single transactions.

items.why: Consistent fee patterns can be used as a fingerprint to link transactions from the same user or wallet.
items.howTo: Manually adjust fees instead of using wallet defaults. Use different fee levels for different transactions.

items.why: Wallet labels and transaction notes can leak sensitive information if your wallet file is compromised.
items.howTo: Avoid labeling transactions with personal information. Regularly clean wallet metadata and export clean copies.
